name: votive deposits

attributes.attribute: received offerings in hopes of a boon

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Votive deposits were a Celtic ritual. The Celts made offerings at holy places. They offered coins, pins, and jewelry. They offered swords, other weapons, and clay sculptures. The sculptures showed divinities or human forms. Each gift went to the power that dwelt in a place. People hoped to win a boon or escape a danger. River beginnings, wells, lakes, and hot springs were favored.

okr.objective: Votive deposits are a Celtic ritual of offering at holy places.
key_results: The Celts made offerings at holy places.
Gifts included coins, pins, jewelry, swords, and weapons.
Clay sculptures showed divinities or human forms.
